name: ia-content-type
thesis: Make the content class the first thing the operator and the admin choose, because it is the first thing they already know: every committed write (113 quest edits, 26 asset creates, 8 AI edits, 1 jutsu create) and capture in the record is keyed by class, the game's staff surface is class-first, and the capability, publish gate, preview path and history support differ per class, so a class-first shell can state truthfully what Forge can do for each class while the cross-class objects that carry lifecycle risk (packages, jobs/recovery, projects) stay cross-class, reachable from every lane, and wear the derived READ ONLY / LIVE WRITE / PUBLISH / RECOVERY band.

navigation_model.name: Content Lanes first: one destination per TNR content class, with cross-type Operations (Home, Packages, Jobs & Recovery, Projects), a gold Content Admin lane and Settings
navigation_model.paragraph: The first level of Forge Next is the set of content classes the game itself is organised by and that every committed manifest and bundle is keyed by: Quests (hosting Quest Studio per RUL-2026-09-12-001), AI, Assets, Jutsu, Items, Bloodlines and Guides (placeholder until K-13/K-29). Each lane is a small vertical product for that class: its capability card (what Forge can capture/create/edit/publish/preview for THIS class, computed from recipes.mjs entities, procedures.mjs and a per-class admin adapter table, never asserted), its records (from the journal, the capture cache and the repository catalogs, zero-live), its packages (manifests in push/ whose parsed plan touches the class), and for Quests the Studio. Everything that is inherently cross-type stays cross-type and is reached from every lane: Home (Command Center), Packages (manifest discovery and preflight, because a manifest may span classes: pack 21 carried 8 asset creates and 10 quest edits, harvest-evidence bundle 1788128500937), Jobs & Recovery (the journal is job-keyed, not class-keyed, and SENT/ORPHANED must be visible from everywhere: SCR-08), Projects (roadmap.json projection), Content Admin (a separate authority lane whose queue and record faces are grouped by the same classes) and Settings/Diagnostics. Operation modes are never destinations: READ ONLY / LIVE WRITE / PUBLISH / RECOVERY are derived from the parsed plan or the journal and shown in the ModeBand above every actionable flow (K-33 derived-only recommendation). On desktop the rail lists the lanes directly; on the phone the bottom navigation is Home · Content · Jobs · More, where Content is the lane grid ordered by recent use, so the phone never scrolls a tab strip (MOB-02) and Admin sits under More until K-03/K-20a rule otherwise.

structural_distinction: Content Operations = the seven content lanes + Packages + Jobs & Recovery + Captures library: blue (read) and crimson (write) constructions; every write is a package (manifest or Studio build) that passes PK-02 preflight and the runner.

Content Admin = its own top-level destination with a gold identity (gold OUTLINE for pending counts and admin rows; solid gold only on the Publish ink button and PUBLISH band, D_VISUAL_SYSTEM tokens --pub/--pub-text); its own queue (A-01), its own record face (A-02) and its own flows (A-03..A-06).

Both share the runner, journal, reconciler and auth gate underneath: an admin edit or publish IS a journaled job with source 'admin' instead of a push/ manifest path, so SENT reconciliation, read-back and INCOMPLETE apply unchanged (R-01).

The same per-class adapter (field allowlist, unhide-gate rule derived from the pin, renderer path) drives L-02 (operator face: manifest/journal/procedure visible) and A-02 (admin face: human fields, preview, publish); the adapter table is a registry projection, not a UI rule table (RB section 4).
admin_never_sees_a_manifest: A-02/A-03 render from a live captured record and the queue entry, never from manifest text; the adapter composes the whole-record update internally (routersA note: no partial PATCH exists for any class).

The journaled admin job's Run view opens in the admin face (human summary, read-back) by default; the manifest it generated, the journal record and the exchange log are under J-05 'Technical' which is collapsed and operator-oriented.
Copy for admin surfaces never names procedure paths (K-19 fix): 'reading an AI record' not 'profile.getAi'.
how_data_moves: Operator runs a package → hidden records created/edited → Forge exports the bundle → operator (or the Studio package gate) writes the queue entry state/review/<slug>.json {class, id, title, change summary, bundle ref, last read-back visibility, review state} through the Contents API on the operator device (needs the PAT the operator already holds; path under state/** so only scrub fires: repo-consumers note 8).

Admin device reads the queue file and the referenced record (public <class>.get returns hidden rows for jutsu/item/bloodline/quest/gameAsset; profile.getAi is protected; guide.get gates drafts) on its own game session; role checks stay server-side (canChangeContent, permissions.ts:22-37).

Admin edit/publish runs through the runner on the admin's own session; the read-back is the durable evidence in the game; whether the admin device also commits a bundle and updates the queue entry is K-15 (recommended (a): no PAT on the admin device; the operator's device reconciles the queue from the next capture or from an exported bundle).
Approval/review state is coordination state in the repository, never live state or canon (K-09, CONTENT_WORKSTREAM stance); Project Workspace renders it beside the roadmap (K-40 pointer).

workflow_mix_evidence: 42 committed bundles / 41 manifests: every write is keyed by content class — quest:edit 113, asset:create 26 (+9 misrouted), ai:edit 8, jutsu:create 1; zero item/bloodline work (harvest-evidence manifest-feature-usage rows).

Captures are keyed by class too: quests.get 150 manifest captures, ai.getAiProfile 28 + profile.getAi 26, gameAsset.get 23, jutsu.get 16; the only cross-class research reads are combat.* (44) which are outside the registry (P-10).

Sessions cluster by class: the mission census → generator → push loop (25/28 → 46), the Forsworn scene-character packs (16 → 16b → 16c), the boss AI audits (40–44), the One Perfect Crop asset probes (push/02–04). An operator arriving at Forge knows which class they are working on before they know which operation.

The game's own staff surface is class-first (/manual/jutsu, /manual/item, /manual/bloodline, /manual/quest, /manual/ai, /manual/asset, /guide: editors evidence), so the Content Admin already thinks in these terms and deep links map 1:1.
risk_rationale: Capability and publish semantics differ PER CLASS, not per operation: hidden on jutsu/item/bloodline/quest/gameAsset (required boolean on item/quest, optional on jutsu/bloodline/gameAsset), published on guides, nothing on AI; unhide gates differ (quest sceneCharacters quests.ts:764-778; jutsu ≥1 effect with appearAnimation AND appearSfx jutsu.ts:762-773; item WEAPON/battle-usable CONSUMABLE item.ts:461-476; bloodline none); history exists for jutsu/item/bloodline/ai/badge/guide but not quest/gameAsset (LOG_TYPES). A class-first IA lets each lane state truthfully what it can do (WFA-13) instead of a global Publish destination that must be re-gated per class anyway.

The cross-class objects (jobs, packages, projects) are exactly the ones that carry lifecycle risk, so they stay cross-class and are reachable from every lane; the class lanes carry no lifecycle state of their own (LaneCard rule: colour and glow, no state).

Mobile ergonomics: 4 bottom tabs (Home · Content · Jobs · More) satisfy MOB-02 without a scrolling strip; the lane grid is one tap; the two highest-frequency journeys (open a package; capture a record) are quick actions on Home so they cost the same 2 taps as in an operation-first model.
frequency_and_risk_rationale.why_not_operation_first: An operation-first level (Capture / Create / Update / Review / Publish) forces the class choice at the second level of every flow and duplicates the per-class capability gating in five places; it also invites the mockup's unverified destinations ('Create Content', 'Edit & Write', 'Validate') to become tabs with nothing behind them (R-16). Operations are better expressed as the derived ModeBand and as verbs on each lane and package.

weaknesses: Rail breadth: 13 desktop destinations (Home, 7 lanes, Packages, Jobs & Recovery, Projects, Content Admin, Settings) against the K-20 advisory of ≤7; mitigated by grouping and a disabled Guides row, but it is more chrome than an operation-first rail.
Phone indirection: the lanes sit one tap behind a Content hub tab; the two dominant journeys are rescued by Home quick actions, but lane switching mid-session costs 2 taps.

Cross-class packages do not belong to any lane; a lane's package list is a filtered view that depends on parsing cached manifest text, which today lives under the game read cache path github.contents (A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP A.5 smell) and must move to its own store.
Lanes are empty on a fresh device until work exists; the answers/ catalogs (GitHub read) give names but no state, and per-class live counts are deliberately not shown (R-03).

Two lanes (Items, Bloodlines) have no committed work and one (Guides) is a placeholder pending K-13/K-17/K-29; a class-first shell makes absent capability visible rather than hiding it, which the director may read as clutter.

Research reads that are not a content class (combat.* battle logs, push/05-06) have no lane; they are parked in the Captures library behind K-06/K-17, which is honest but not prominent for a workflow that ran twice in the last week on Builder.

The ad-hoc 'Read live' on a record (L-02) is a new capability outside the manifest model; if the director keeps reads manifest-only, lanes lose their most natural verb and the capture journey stays 4-5 taps via a capture-only package.

Admin per-class adapters (allowlist, gate rule, renderer) are seven pieces of work before the admin lane is fully truthful; the queue file (K-09) and PAT model (K-15) must be ruled before A-01 is more than a placeholder.
A manifest that flips hidden:false is shown as LIVE WRITE with a 'publishes' chip rather than PUBLISH mode; the director may prefer the stricter reading (K-21).
No browser measurement: 13-row rail height, 4-tab bottom nav with badges, and lane-grid ordering are Inferred until the user's smoke.

A class-first shell promises a Records list per lane, but the live source for that list (paged, filtered <class>.getAll with hidden:true) is exactly the capability Forge refuses today (P-11 GAP, retirement blocker, gate G-03; CachedReader.list handles name paths only, reader.mjs:73-86). Until G-03 passes, every lane Records segment and the admin queue A-01 are backed by the repository catalogs, the journal and the capture cache, not by a live draft list, so the model's most natural screen is the one carrying the largest capability debt.
